The diagram at the top left shows the location of the kidneys in the abdominal cavity. This illustration comprehensively demonstrates the gross anatomical organization of the kidney and its major structural divisions.

u5.title: The Kidney Filters the Blood and Removes Waste Materials
u5.description: A comprehensive diagram showing the detailed internal anatomy of the kidney and the nephron structure responsible for blood filtration. The left side shows the overall kidney anatomy with labels for calyces, renal pelvis, renal artery, renal vein, ureter, renal cortex, and renal medulla. The right side provides a magnified view of a single nephron (the functional filtration unit) showing all major components in their functional relationships: the glomerulus (network of blood capillaries where filtration occurs), renal corpuscle (containing glomerulus and Bowman's capsule), proximal convoluted tubule (site of selective reabsorption), loop of Henle (U-shaped region for water reabsorption), distal convoluted tubule (further selective reabsorption), collecting duct (final concentration of urine). The diagram shows blood vessels including the renal artery, efferent arteriole, and vein. Color coding distinguishes different regions and processes: red for arteries bringing blood, blue for veins draining blood, and tan/brown for tubular structures. This illustration demonstrates how the kidney's microscopic structure enables its macroscopic function of blood filtration and urine production.

u5.title: The Liver is One of the Most Active Organs in the Body
u5.description: A detailed anatomical illustration showing the structure and position of the liver and its relationships to adjacent organs and structures. The diagram displays the liver (in dark red/brown) as the largest internal organ in the abdominal cavity with extensive blood vessel networks visible on its surface (shown in red for arteries and blue for veins). The illustration identifies numerous structures: right hepatic duct and left hepatic duct (draining bile from the liver), common hepatic duct (collecting bile from both sides), hepatic artery (bringing blood to the liver in red), hepatic portal vein (bringing nutrient-rich blood from the intestine in blue), gallbladder (small green structure storing bile), cystic duct (connecting gallbladder to hepatic system), common bile duct (conveying bile to the duodenum), stomach (visible below), pancreas (to the left of the stomach, in tan), duodenum (first portion of small intestine), and spleen (purple structure to the right). The illustration demonstrates the liver's complex vascular anatomy and its extensive connections to the digestive system, showing how the liver receives blood from two sources (hepatic artery and hepatic portal vein) and drains bile through the biliary system.

u6.title: Progressive Increase of Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide Concentrations Since 1750
u6.description: A dual-axis line graph showing the correlation between atmospheric CO2 and emissions from 1750 to 2020. The pink line tracks atmospheric CO2 (left axis, in parts per million), rising from approximately 280 ppm to over 400 ppm. The blue line tracks annual CO2 emissions (right axis, in billions of tons), showing a sharp exponential increase starting around 1950. Data is sourced from NOAA, ETHZ, and Our World in Data.

u6.title: Ethiopia’s Annual CO2 Emission
u6.description: A line graph showing Ethiopia's carbon dioxide emissions from 1800 to 2019. Emissions remain near zero until approximately 1950, followed by a steady increase that turns into a sharp, rapid spike after the year 2000, reaching over 16 million tons (t) by 2019.

u6.title: Climate Change and its Potential Impacts on Agriculture
u6.description: A conceptual diagram centered on 'Climate Change' (defined by increased temperature and CO2). Eight surrounding boxes illustrate negative agricultural consequences: decreased soil fertility, increased desertification, higher crop water requirements, lower crop productivity, reduced production, lower farm net revenue, decreased sufficiency rates, and an increased production gap.

u6.title: Climate Policy Timeline
u6.description: A horizontal timeline tracking major international climate agreements and organizations from 1988 to 2015. Key milestones include the start of the IPCC (1988), the establishment and entry into force of the UNFCCC (1992/1994), the adoption of the Kyoto Protocol (1997) and its start (2008), the introduction of REDD (2005), and major COP summits in Bali, Copenhagen, Cancun, and Durban.

u6.title: Environmental Cause and Effect Flowchart
u6.description: A two-part flowchart for completion. The top sequence links unknown cause (a) to decreased ozone levels, which leads to unknown effect (b), resulting in harmful mutations and a secondary unknown effect (c). The bottom sequence links the burning of fossil fuels to an unknown atmospheric change (d), which leads to increased global temperatures, resulting in two distinct unknown environmental consequences (e and f).
